validation.name: pk_hit
validation.sql: SELECT score FROM items WHERE id = $1

validation.name: indexed_join
validation.sql: SELECT a.label, b.score FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.id = a.id AND b.bucket <> 3 WHERE a.id = $1 ORDER BY b.id LIMIT 1

validation.name: three_table_join
validation.sql: SELECT a.id, b.score, c.label FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.id = a.id JOIN items c ON c.id = b.id WHERE a.id = $1 AND b.id = $1 AND c.id = $1 ORDER BY a.id

validation.name: three_table_join_miss
validation.sql: SELECT a.id, b.score, c.label FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.id = a.id JOIN items c ON c.id = b.id WHERE a.id = $1 AND b.id = $1 AND c.id = $1 ORDER BY a.id

validation.name: three_table_join_range
validation.sql: SELECT a.id, b.score, c.label FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.id = a.id JOIN items c ON c.id = b.id WHERE a.id < $1 AND b.id < $1 AND c.id < $1 ORDER BY a.id

validation.name: three_table_computed_key
validation.sql: SELECT a.id, b.score, c.label FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.id = a.id % 10 JOIN items c ON c.id = b.id WHERE a.id = $1 AND b.id < 10 AND c.id < 10 ORDER BY a.id

validation.name: four_table_join
validation.sql: SELECT a.id, b.score, c.label, d.bucket FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.id = a.id JOIN items c ON c.id = b.id JOIN items d ON d.id = c.id WHERE a.id = $1 AND b.id = $1 AND c.id = $1 AND d.id = $1 ORDER BY a.id

validation.name: three_table_left_fence
validation.sql: SELECT a.id, b.score, c.label FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.id = a.id LEFT JOIN items c ON c.id = b.id AND c.bucket <> 3 WHERE a.id = $1 AND b.id = $1 ORDER BY a.id

notes: Adaptive follow-up to the original ZJIT prepared three-table regression; original reports remain primary.
All nine jobs retain their original order, fixture, parameter schedule, validation and batch sizes.
Only the target warmup differs between short and long plans. Each batch restarts at parameter index zero.
No elapsed query times are measured. Statistics collection, its allocations and the extra replay frames may affect JIT/GC behavior.
Numeric ZJIT and GC counters are sampled outside target warmup and batch loops; GC.stat time is milliseconds and GC.total_time is nanoseconds.
Counter changes can identify activity in this replay but do not establish the cause of an uninstrumented timing difference.
